chunks: Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah reported to me, from a group of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from 'Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan—all of them—from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam:
He said: I saw Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) offering condolences (ta'ziyah) before the burial and after it.
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible in Shia jurisprudence to offer condolences (ta'ziyah) both before and after burial?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar records Hisham ibn al-Hakam's eyewitness account of Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kazim (peace be upon him) offering condolences (ta'ziyah) both before and after the burial of the deceased. In Shia jurisprudence, this narrated action (fi'l) of the Imam constitutes legal evidence establishing that ta'ziyah is a sunnah permissible at both times, not restricted to after burial alone.
